claim: BBS10 acts with CCT; is the ATPase supplied in trans?
finding: BBS6, BBS10 and BBS12 form a complex with CCT/TRiC and mediate BBSome assembly; CCT activity is essential for BBSome assembly; CCT knockdown in zebrafish gives BBS phenotypes
conf: high for the interaction; the paper does not assay BBS10 nucleotide binding or turnover

claim: BBS10 function is BBSome assembly, not folding catalysis
finding: The BBS-chaperonin complex contributes to BBS7 stability; BBSome assembles sequentially from a BBS7-BBS2-BBS9 core
conf: moderate; stability readout cannot separate a catalytic from a scaffolding contribution

claim: Loss of the catalytic aspartate abolishes hydrolysis but not binding
finding: GroEL D398A retains <2% of wild-type ATP hydrolysis but is not deficient in ATP binding; D52A retains ~20%; D52A/D398A retains <0.01%
context: E. coli GroEL, purified protein ATPase assay
conf: high for GroEL; transfer to BBS10 is inference from structural equivalence

claim: Chaperonin-like BBS proteins are not ATP-dependent folding machines
finding: BBS6, BBS10 and BBS12 are believed to conserve neither the ATP-dependent folding activity of canonical CCT chaperonins nor the ability to form CCT-like oligomeric complexes
context: review of human BBS genetics and cell biology

claim: Chaperonin function of BBS6/10/12 is settled
finding: Chaperonin function of BBS6, BBS10 and BBS12 is debated; they are required for initial BBSome assembly in vitro
conf: review-level; records the unresolved state rather than resolving it

claim: An ATP-sized pocket is assembled in the BBS10 equatorial domain
finding: TM-score 0.836 to Mm-cpn 3RUW chain A; transplanted ADP-AlF3-Mg contacts 122 BBS10 heavy atoms within 5 A (CCT5 110, BBS6 101, BBS12 124) with only 10 atoms closer than 2.5 A, so the cavity is open and not occluded; adenine/ribose subsite identity 0.67, inside the CCT1-CCT8 range 0.42-0.75
context: AlphaFold model, pLDDT 88-96 over the site
conf: prediction from a model, not an experimental BBS10 structure; no BBS10 structure exists in the PDB

claim: BBS10 retains the group II catalytic machinery
finding: 1 of 6 catalytic/Mg positions identical to Mm-cpn (D81 only); GDGTT phosphate loop reads GDGAKT (79-85); no Asp or Glu side chain within 7.27 A of the transplanted Mg/AlF3 centre in any alignment register, against 3.40 A for Mm-cpn D386 and 4.13 A for CCT5 D404
context: AlphaFold Q8TAM1 vs 3RUW, CCT1-CCT8, BBS6, BBS12
conf: high internal consistency; depends on the AlphaFold apo conformation being close to the nucleotide-bound state

claim: The substitutions are fixed, and the pocket is under selection
finding: Site positions median identity 0.931 vs background 0.533 (Mann-Whitney p=3.0e-05, r=0.553); catalytic-Asp column is Gly in 12/15 and Asp in 0/15; Lys at the Mm-cpn T94 column in 15/15; basic residue at the catalytic-Lys column in 15/15
context: 15 full-length vertebrate orthologs, 7 truncated models flagged
conf: high; Ensembl gene models of variable quality, truncated ones excluded from scoring

claim: Human BBS10 is representative of the family at every site position
finding: Human Asn-50 at the NDG-loop aspartate position is primate-specific; 13 of 14 non-primate orthologs carry Asp (RDGG context) and marmoset shares the human RNGG
conf: high for the column; functional consequence is inference

claim: Existing GO:0005524 on BBS10 reflects evidence
finding: GO:0005524 on BBS10, BBS6 and BBS12 is IEA from InterPro GO_REF:0000002 via PF00118 / IPR002423; no GO:0016887, GO:0140662 or GO:0044183 on any of the three; BBS10 has 0 EXP and 0 IDA annotations against 4 EXP and 9 IDA for CCT4
context: human UniProt accessions Q8TAM1, Q9NPJ1, Q6ZW61, P50991
conf: high; database state at the retrieval date
